title: Stage 3: Rebase and squash for review
summary: 14:00. Your branch has five commits, two of them fixes to earlier ones. Shape it into a clean story before you request review.

steps.title: Briefing
body: b2 Show coupon field at checkout
e5 fixup! Show coupon field at checkout
You made c3 and e5 with `git commit --fixup=<hash>`, which writes the special subject `fixup! <target subject>`. Now:
Git pre-arranges the todo list: each `fixup!` commit moves directly under its target, with the verb `fixup`. You only need to decide what to do with `wip`.

steps.prompt: Write the todo list `git rebase -i --autosquash` opens, before you change anything (one line per commit, `verb hash subject`).
answer: fixup c3 fixup! Add percentage coupons (SHOP-142)
pick b2 Show coupon field at checkout
fixup e5 fixup! Show coupon field at checkout
steps.explain: Each `fixup!` commit is moved right after the commit whose subject it names, and gets the verb `fixup`. Other commits keep their order.

steps.prompt: `d4 wip` contains a useful validation change for the coupon field. What is the best edit to the todo?
options: Move it under `b2` and change it to `fixup` (or `squash` if its message adds something)
steps.explain: Its change belongs to the coupon-field commit. Dropping would lose code; keeping *wip* leaves an unreviewable commit.

steps.prompt: After your edited rebase, how many commits does `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` print? (A number.)
code: fixup c3 fixup! Add percentage coupons (SHOP-142)
pick b2 Show coupon field at checkout
fixup e5 fixup! Show coupon field at checkout
steps.explain: Two picks, everything else melted into them: one commit for the logic, one for the UI. Exactly the two-commit story a reviewer wants.

steps.prompt: Now that the branch is rewritten: fine or not?
items: Telling the reviewer you rewrote the branch
steps.explain: A plain push is rejected (the old tip is no longer an ancestor). `--force` would overwrite a reviewer's pushed suggestion without warning.

steps.title: Implement --autosquash
prompt: Write `Autosquash(List<(string Hash, string Subject)> commits)` that produces the todo list `git rebase -i --autosquash` would open. `commits` are oldest first.

- A commit whose subject starts with `fixup! ` or `squash! ` is moved directly after the commit whose subject equals the rest (after the prefix), with the verb `fixup` or `squash`. Several fixups for one target keep their original order.
- All other commits are `pick`, in their original order.
starter: static List<string> Autosquash(List<(string Hash, string Subject)> commits)
solution: static List<string> Autosquash(List<(string Hash, string Subject)> commits)
hints: Loop over the other commits; after adding each `pick`, add every fixup that targets its subject.
The target is the subject after `fixup! ` (7 characters) or `squash! ` (8 characters).
template: var dojoC = new List<(string Hash, string Subject)> {
("a1", "Add percentage coupons"), ("b2", "Show coupon field"), ("c3", "fixup! Add percentage coupons"),
("d4", "wip"), ("e5", "squash! Show coupon field"), ("f6", "fixup! Add percentage coupons") };
"pick a1 Add percentage coupons", "fixup c3 fixup! Add percentage coupons", "fixup f6 fixup! Add percentage coupons",
"pick b2 Show coupon field", "squash e5 squash! Show coupon field", "pick d4 wip" }, Autosquash(dojoC));
Dojo.Eq("no fixups", new List<string> { "pick x one", "pick y two" }, Autosquash(new() { ("x", "one"), ("y", "two") }));
